akhfash:13-13.t:
He said ﴿مَّا لَكُمْ لاَ تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَاراً﴾, that is: you do not fear Allah's grandeur. "الرَّجاء" here is fear, and "الوَقار" is grandeur. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-second verse cited as evidence]:
إِذَا لَسَعَتْهُ النَحْلُ لَمْ يَرْجُ لَسْعَهَا * [وخَالَفَها في بَيْتِ نوبٍ عَواسِلِ]
(When the bees sting him he does not fear their sting, and he comes at them in the home of honey-making swarms.)

akhfash:14-14.t: And He said ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَاراً﴾: at one stage a clinging clot (عَلَقَة) and at another stage a lump of flesh (مُضْغَة).

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿وَجَعَلَ ٱلْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُوراً﴾: this is only — and Allah knows best — in accordance with the speech of the Arabs, for the moon is only in the lowest heaven, according to what has been mentioned; just as you say "أَتَيْتُ بني تَمِيم" ("I came to Banū Tamīm") when you only came to some of them.

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَرْضِ نَبَاتاً﴾: He made "النَّبَات" the maṣdar (verbal noun), whereas the maṣdar is "الإِنْبات", because this indicates the meaning.

akhfash:20-20.t: And He said ﴿سُبُلاً فِجَاجاً﴾: its singular is "الفَجُّ", which is the road.

akhfash:24-24.t: And He said ﴿وَلاَ تَزِدِ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾ because this is from the words of Noah, an imprecation against them.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿نُوحاً﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿إِلى قَوْمِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَنْ أَنْذِرْ﴾ an explicative particle (ḥarf tafsīr), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿قَوْمَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and its mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle. ﴿قَوْمِ إِنِّي﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person, and the vocative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and inna and its noun. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿نَذِيرٌ﴾ khabar of inna. ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the nominal clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an is an explicative particle (ḥarf tafsīr), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the Name of Majesty is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to اعبدوا.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿يَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the response to the request, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to the verb, and they function as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿إِلى أَجَلٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مُسَمًّى﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿إِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ﴾ inna and its noun, annexed to the Name of Majesty. ﴿إِذا جاءَ﴾ idhā is a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿لا يُؤَخَّرُ﴾ negative, and a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; idhā together with its protasis and apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a conditional particle that does not make jussive. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause «كنتم..» is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:5-6.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, omitted for lightness; the vocative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿قَوْمِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿لَيْلًا﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿وَنَهاراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ليلا. ﴿فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the hāʾ is its first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿دُعائِي﴾ a postponed fāʿil. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿فِراراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَإِنِّي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and inna and its noun. ﴿كُلَّما دَعَوْتُهُمْ﴾ kullamā is a conditional particle that does not make jussive, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿لِتَغْفِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb تغفر. ﴿جَعَلُوا أَصابِعَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِي آذانِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb, and they stand in the place of the second object; the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاسْتَغْشَوْا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جعلوا. ﴿ثِيابَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَصَرُّوا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ conjoined to استغشوا. ﴿اسْتِكْباراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

daas-irab:8-9.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُهُمْ﴾ thumma is a conjunction, and inna and its noun, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿جِهاراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿إِنِّي أَعْلَنْتُ﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to أعلنت لهم. ﴿إِسْراراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq.

daas-irab:10-11.t: ﴿فَقُلْتُ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿اسْتَغْفِرُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿رَبَّكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna [and] its noun. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun is latent (mustatir). ﴿غَفَّاراً﴾ khabar (predicate) of kāna; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿يُرْسِلِ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿السَّماءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِدْراراً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the response to the request, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يرسل, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِأَمْوالٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَبَنِينَ﴾ conjoined to أموال. ﴿وَيَجْعَلْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ أَنْهاراً﴾ parsed like the preceding one.

daas-irab:13-14.t: ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لا تَرْجُونَ﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَقاراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl. ﴿قَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ﴾ a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَطْواراً﴾ ḥāl; the clause is a ḥāl clause.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَوْا﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿سَماواتٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿طِباقاً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of سبع; the clause خلق stands in place of the two objects of تروا.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿وَجَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْقَمَرَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿نُوراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it, and what follows it is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:17-18.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject), and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿نَباتاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ﴾ thumma is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ﴾ conjoined to يعيدكم. ﴿إِخْراجاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq.

daas-irab:19-20.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject), and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِساطاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿لِتَسْلُكُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to جعل. ﴿مِنْها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سُبُلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِجاجاً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); فجاجا means wide.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿قالَ نُوحٌ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, omitted for lightness. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the vocative clause with what follows it is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿لَمْ يَزِدْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مالُهُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿وَوَلَدُهُ﴾ conjoined to ماله. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿خَساراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وَمَكَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مَكْراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿كُبَّاراً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿لا تَذَرُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil, and the nūn is for emphasis. ﴿آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلا تَذَرُنَّ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَدًّا﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and what follows it is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا﴾ qad is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿كَثِيراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَلا تَزِدِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lā, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ضَلالًا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿مِمَّا﴾ min is a preposition. ﴿ما﴾ redundant (zāʾida). ﴿خَطِيئاتِهِمْ﴾ genitive (majrūr) by min, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿أُغْرِقُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَأُدْخِلُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أغرقوا. ﴿ناراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ من دون is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَنْصاراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿وَقالَ نُوحٌ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿رَبِّ لا تَذَرْ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, omitted for lightness, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lā, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلَى الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿دَيَّاراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the vocative clause and the verbal clause are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿إِنْ تَذَرْهُمْ﴾ in is a conditional particle that makes jussive, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يُضِلُّوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿عِبادَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the condition and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of إنك, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلا يَلِدُوا﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿فاجِراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَفَّاراً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿رَبِّ اغْفِرْ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, omitted for lightness, and a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ) whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَلِوالِدَيَّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to لي. ﴿وَلِمَنْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also conjoined [to it]. ﴿دَخَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بَيْتِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مُؤْمِناً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا تَزِدِ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lā, whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿تَباراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَنْ أَنذِرْ قَوْمَكَ﴾.
That is: We sent him with the warning. (أن) is in the position of the accusative, because you have dropped the preposition from it. Had it been إنا أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه أنذر قومك, without أن, [it would have been correct], because "sending" is in origin a [kind of] saying; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is so, without أن.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾.
Years of hardship had pressed hard on them and carried off their wealth because the rain had ceased, and their women had stopped bearing children; so He said: ﴿وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿مَّا لَكُمْ لاَ تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَاراً﴾. That is: you do not fear Allah's majesty.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَاراً﴾.
A drop of sperm, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then bone.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقاً﴾.
If you wish, you may make طباق [217/b] accusative by the verb, i.e.: He created them layered one upon another; and if you wish, you may make it an adjective (naʿt) of السبع, not by the verb. Had it been سبع سمواتٍ طباقٍ in the genitive, it would be a good way, as is read: "ثِيابُ سُنْدسٍ خُضْرٍ" and "خضرٌ".

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ ٱلْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُوراً﴾.
It is mentioned that the back of the sun lights up the heavens adjacent to it, and its face lights up for the people of the earth; and likewise the moon. The meaning is: He made the sun and the moon a light in the heavens and the earth.

farraa:20-21.t:
His saying: ﴿سُبُلاً فِجَاجاً﴾.
Paths; its singular is فج, and they are wide roads.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Hushaym told me, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, that he read: ﴿مَالُهُ وَوَلَدُهُ﴾.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَكَرُواْ مَكْراً كُبَّاراً﴾.
الكُبَّار means الكبير (great); and the Arabs say كُبَار.
They say: رجل حُسَّان جُمَّال (a very handsome, very beautiful man) with doubling, and حُسَان جُمَال light, in many of its like.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَذَرُنَّ وَدّاً وَلاَ سُوَاعاً﴾.
These are gods that Iblīs made for them. The readers differed over ودّ: the people of Medina read (وُدًّا) with ḍamma, and al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read (وَدًّا) with fatḥa.
They did not make (يَغُوثَ، ويَعُوقَ) fully declinable (lam yujrū), because they have an added yāʾ. Any proper noun that has [an added] yāʾ, tāʾ or alif is not made fully declinable; among them: يَملِك, يزيد, يعمَر, تغلب and أحمد. These are not made declinable because of what is added in them. Had they been made declinable because of their frequent use as names, it would be correct; and had they been made declinable as if intended as indefinite, that too would be correct.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "ولا تَذَرُنَّ وَدَّا ولا سُواعاً ويَغوثاً ويَعَوقاً ونَسْراً", with alif [i.e. with tanwīn]. ﴿وقَدْ أَضَلُّوا كثيرا﴾: He is saying: many people have gone astray through these idols. Had it been said: وقد أضلّت كثيرا or أضللن, it would be correct.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿مِّمَّا خَطِيۤئَاتِهِمْ﴾.
The Arabs make (ما) a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) in what is intended in the manner of a conditional (jazāʾ), as if you said: إن خطيئاتهم ما أغرقوا (it was because of their sins that they were drowned); and that is how I saw it in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh, and its being put after is evidence of the conditional manner. Similar to it in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿أىَّ الأجَلَيْنِ ما قضيتُ فلا عُدْوانَ عَلَىّ﴾. Do you not see that you say: حيثما تكن أكن (wherever you are, I will be) and مهما تقل أقلْ (whatever you say, I will say)? Of that is: ﴿أَيًّا مَّا تَدْعُو فَلَه الأَسْماءُ الحسنى﴾: the conditional is joined with ما. But when it is a question they do not join it with ما; they say: كيف تصنع؟ (how do you act?) and أين تذهب؟ (where are you going?). When it is a question it is not joined with ما; when it is a conditional, it is joined, and joining is also omitted.
[Translator's note: «إن خطيئاتهم ما أغرقوا» is as printed; the expected illustrative form is «من خطيئاتهم ما أغرقوا».]

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿دَيَّاراً﴾.
It is from دُرت (I went round), but it is [on the pattern] fayʿāl from الدوران, just as ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb read: ﴿اللهُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ الْحَىُّ الْقَيّامُ﴾, which is from قمتُ.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى﴾.
[A term] named among you, which you know: He will not cause you to die by drowning, burning or killing. There is no proof in this for the Qadarites, because He only meant: named among you. Similar to it: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِى يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عليه﴾: [easier] in your estimation, according to your knowledge.
His saying: ﴿يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾.
من can be for the whole of what it applies to, or for part of it. As for "part", it is your saying: اشتريت من عبيدك (I bought some of your slaves); as for "the whole", it is your saying: رَوِيت من مائك (I quenched my thirst from your water). When it is in a position of totality, it is as if من were عن, as you say: اشتكيت من ماء شربته and عن ماء شربته (I fell ill from water I drank). It is as if in speech it were: يغفر لكم عن أذنابكم and من أذنابكم.
[Translator's note: «أذنابكم» is as printed (twice), evidently for «ذنوبكم» ("your sins").]

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿لَيْلاً وَنَهَاراً﴾.
That is: I called them in every way, secretly and openly.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَصَرُّواْ﴾.
That is: they kept silently to their polytheism, ﴿وَٱسْتَكْبَرُواْ﴾ [and were too proud] to believe.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Nūḥ
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنّا أرْسَلْنا نُوحًا إلى قَوْمِهِ أنْ أنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يَأْتِيَهم عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾ ("Indeed, We sent Noah to his people: Warn your people before a painful punishment comes to them"). «أنْ» is in the position of an accusative by «أرْسَلْنا», because the original is «بِأنْ أنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ» ("with: warn your people"); when the bāʾ was dropped, the verb reached «أنْ» and put it in the accusative (accusative by removal of the preposition). Some people whose knowledge is approved said that the position of the like of it is genitive even though the bāʾ has dropped, because with «أنْ» the dropping of the bāʾ is acceptable, whereas the bāʾ is not dropped from the maṣdar (verbal noun): if you said «إنِّي أرْسَلْتُكَ بِالإنْذارِ والتَّهَدُّدِ» ("I sent you with warning and threatening"), it would not be permissible to say «إنِّي أرْسَلْتُكَ الإنْذارَ والتَّهَدُّدَ»; but if you said «إنِّي أرْسَلْتُكَ بِأنْ تُنْذِرَ وأنْ تُهَدِّدَ», then «إنِّي أرْسَلْتُكَ أنْ تُنْذِرَ وأنْ تُهَدِّدَ» would be permissible. The root meaning of «الإنْذار» in the language is informing of something to be feared, so that one is wary of it and does not expose oneself to it. It is also possible that «أنْ» is explicative (tafsīriyya) of what he was sent with, so the meaning would be: "Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, namely: warn your people."

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكم مِدْرارًا﴾ ("He will send the sky upon you in abundant showers"). It was said that they had suffered drought, so he informed them that their belief in Allah would bring them, together with an ample share in the Hereafter, fertility and wealth in this world. ﴿مِدْرارًا﴾: abundant in flow, i.e. abundant in rain.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
﴿وَيُمْدِدْكم بِأمْوالٍ وبَنِينَ﴾ ("and give you increase in wealth and sons"): He will give you the adornment of this world, which is wealth and sons.
﴿وَيَجْعَلْ لَكم جَنّاتٍ﴾ ("and provide for you gardens"), i.e. orchards.

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ما لَكم لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وقارًا﴾ ("What is the matter with you that you do not hope for waqār from Allah?"). It was said: "What is the matter with you that you do not fear the majesty of Allah?!" And it was said: "You do not hope for an outcome." Its true sense — and Allah knows best — is: what is the matter with you that you do not hope for the outcome of faith and so affirm the oneness of Allah, when He has placed for you in yourselves a sign pointing to His oneness — His creating you, and His creating the heavens and the earths, the sun and the moon? So He said: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَقَكم أطْوارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 14] ("while He has created you in stages"), i.e. stage after stage: He moved you from state to state and from one aspect of creation to another. He created you from dust, then from a drop of sperm, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh; then He made the lump bone and clothed the bone with flesh.

zajjaj:15-15.t: Then He made them acknowledge, saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ طِباقًا﴾ ("Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens in layers?"). ﴿طِباقًا﴾ is accusative on two lines: one of them is "corresponding in layers (muṭābaqatan ṭibāqan)" [i.e. as a maṣdar]; the other is as a naʿt (adjective) of «سَبْعَ», i.e. "He created seven possessing layers."

zajjaj:16-16.t:
﴿وَجَعَلَ القَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا﴾ ("and made the moon therein a light"). The scholars of Arabic said: it may be [that the moon is] in the lowest heaven, and ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ ("in them") was said because they are like a single thing. It has come in the exegesis that the face of the sun shines for the people of the earth from its back and its nape, and it shines for the people of the heavens; and likewise the moon.
[Translator's note: the source reads «يُضِيءُ لِأهْلِ الأرْضِ مِن ظَهْرِها، وقَفاها»; the usual form of this report is that its face shines for the people of the heavens and its back for the people of the earth, so the text may be disturbed. Translated as written.]

zajjaj:17-17.t:
﴿واللَّهُ أنْبَتَكم مِنَ الأرْضِ نَباتًا﴾ ("And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth a growth"): ﴿نَباتًا﴾ is construed, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), according to the meaning, because the meaning of «أنْبَتَكُمْ» is "He made you grow a growth (nabātan)". [Using] the maṣdar on the wording "He caused you to grow a causing-to-grow (inbātan)" and "a growth (nabātan)" — [the latter] is more eloquent in meaning.
[Translator's note: the final sentence is elliptical in the Arabic («والمَصْدَرُ عَلى لَفْظِ "أنْبَتَكم إنْباتًا، ونَباتًا"، أبْلَغُ في المَعْنى»); the bracketed words reflect one reading of it.]

zajjaj:2-3.t: ﴿قالَ يا قَوْمِ إنِّي لَكم نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ ﴿أنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ واتَّقُوهُ وأطِيعُونِ﴾ ("He said: O my people, I am to you a clear warner, [saying]: Worship Allah, fear Him and obey me"). Allah sent Noah and all the prophets with the command to worship Him, to prefer fearing Him, and to obey His messengers.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿لِتَسْلُكُوا مِنها سُبُلا فِجاجًا﴾ ("that you may follow therein broad roads"), i.e. clear paths.

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿وَوَلَدُهُ﴾ ("and his children"); it is also read «وَوُلْدُهُ». «الوَلَد» and «الوُلْد» have the same meaning, like «العَرَب» and «العُرْب», «العَجَم» and «العُجْم».

zajjaj:22-22.t: His saying ﴿وَمَكَرُوا مَكْرًا كُبّارًا﴾ ("And they plotted a tremendous plot"): one says «مَكْرٌ كَبِيرٌ», «كُبّارٌ» and «كِبّارٌ» with one meaning.

zajjaj:23-23.t:
﴿وَقالُوا لا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكم ولا تَذَرُنَّ ودًّا ولا سُواعًا﴾ ("And they said: Never leave your gods, and never leave Wadd, nor Suwāʿ"); it was also read «وُدًّا» with ḍamma on the wāw; ﴿وَلا يَغُوثَ ويَعُوقَ ونَسْرًا﴾ ("nor Yaghūth, Yaʿūq and Nasr"). These are five idols that existed among the people of Noah, which they worshipped; then they passed to the Arabs.
Wadd belonged to Kalb, Suwāʿ belonged to Hamdān, Yaghūth belonged to Madhḥij, and Nasr belonged to Ḥimyar.
[Translator's note: the source does not mention which tribe Yaʿūq belonged to, although it speaks of five idols.]
It was also read «يَغُوثًا ويَعُوقًا». «يَغُوث» and «يَعُوق» are diptotes (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), because they are on the pattern of a verb and they are definite. The reading which the readers and the Muṣḥaf follow is without nunation (tark al-ṣarf), and there is no alif in «يَغُوثَ» and «يَعُوقَ» in the written text; therefore it should only be read without nunation. Those who gave them nunation treated these two names as mostly declinable, since for them the basic state of nouns is declinability; or they treated them as indefinite even though they are definite, as though they said: "and never leave any idol of your idols". It should not be read so, because it contradicts the Muṣḥaf.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿مِمّا خَطِيئاتِهِمْ﴾ ("Because of their sins"); it is also read «مِمّا خَطاياهُمْ». «خَطِيئَة» has the plurals «خَطايا» and «خَطِيئات». We have explained that earlier in the book.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿وَقالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ لا تَذَرْ عَلى الأرْضِ مِنَ الكافِرِينَ دَيّارًا﴾ ("And Noah said: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any inhabitant from among the unbelievers"). «دَيّارًا» has the meaning of «أحَدًا» ("anyone"); one says «ما في الدّارِ أحَدٌ، وما بِها دَيّارٌ» ("there is no one in the house, there is no inhabitant in it"). Its original form is «دَيْوار», on the pattern fayʿāl; the wāw was changed into yāʾ, and one was assimilated into the other. Noah (peace be upon him) invoked against them only because Allah, Majestic and Exalted, revealed to him ﴿أنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إلا مَن قَدْ آمَنَ﴾ [Hūd: 36] ("that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed").

zajjaj:28-28.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِنًا﴾ ("and whoever enters my house a believer"): they said «بَيْتِيَ» means "my place of prayer (masjid)". If you wish, you may make the yāʾ quiescent, and if you wish, you may give it fatḥa.
And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَزِدِ الظّالِمِينَ إلا تَبارًا﴾ ("and do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction"): its meaning — "except in tabār": «التَّبار» is destruction. Everything destroyed has been «تُبِّرَ»; therefore everything broken up is called «تِبْر».

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿يَغْفِرْ لَكم مِن ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ ("He will forgive you of your sins"): «يَغْفِرْ» is jussive (majzūm), the answer to the imperative: "Worship Allah, fear Him and obey me — He will forgive you of your sins." All the Basran grammarians — except Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ — do not assimilate the rāʾ into the lām; they do not permit «يَغْفِر لَّكُمْ». Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ holds the assimilation to be permissible. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh held that the rāʾ is a trilled (mukarrar) letter: whenever it is assimilated into the lām, its trill is lost and the letter is impaired. What is heard from the Arabs, and what the readers read, is pronouncing the rāʾ distinctly. The meaning of ﴿مِن ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ here is: "He will forgive you your sins"; «مِن» came in to single out the sins from all other things, not to make the sins partial. Similar to it is His saying ﴿فاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأوْثانِ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 30] ("So avoid the filth of idols"), meaning: avoid the filth which is the idols; the filth here is not some of the idols.
And His saying: ﴿وَيُؤَخِّرْكم إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمًّى إنَّ أجَلَ اللَّهِ إذا جاءَ لا يُؤَخَّرُ﴾ ("and He will defer you to a specified term; indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, is not deferred") means: fear Allah and obey me, and He will defer you from the punishment, i.e. He will defer you so that you die other than by the death of those uprooted by punishment. Then He said: ﴿إنَّ أجَلَ اللَّهِ إذا جاءَ لا يُؤَخَّرُ﴾, meaning: when the term of death comes it is not deferred, whether by punishment or by uprooting.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿جَعَلُوا أصابِعَهم في آذانِهِمْ واسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ﴾ ("they put their fingers in their ears and covered themselves with their garments"): it was said that they used to stop up their ears and cover their faces so as not to hear his words, and to go to extremes in turning away from him by covering their faces.
And His saying: ﴿وَأصَرُّوا﴾ ("and they persisted"): they persisted and had no intention of repenting of it. ﴿واسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ ("and they were arrogant"): pride kept them from following Noah. The evidence for that is His saying: ﴿أنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ واتَّبَعَكَ الأرْذَلُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 111] ("Shall we believe you while the lowest follow you?").

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿إنِّي دَعَوْتُهم جِهارًا﴾ ("Then I called them openly"), i.e. I called them, making the call manifest to them. «جِهارًا» is accusative: a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "I called them, being open in calling to the oneness of Allah and fear of Him."

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إنِّي أعْلَنْتُ لَهم وأسْرَرْتُ لَهم إسْرارًا﴾ ("Then I announced to them publicly and confided to them secretly"), i.e. I mixed for them calling them in public with calling in secret. ﴿فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكم إنَّهُ كانَ غَفّارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 10] ("And I said: Ask forgiveness of your Lord; indeed, He is ever Forgiving"), i.e. seek your Lord's forgiveness.
